interpretation.label: grounding_real_but_not_load_bearing

preconditions.name: worldeffect_groundable_from_zworld
preconditions.description: ARM_1 median grounding MSE onto the realised next-world-state (unit-variance target; 1.0 = no fit). <= ceiling => z_world carries enough world-effect information for O to be grounded; > ceiling => a SUBSTRATE limit (z_world under-informative), not an objective failure.
preconditions.control: ARM_2 (shuffled target) fits at ~1.0 -- the no-real-structure baseline

preconditions.name: arm1_state_dependence_acquired
preconditions.description: ARM_1 median r2_explained_by_action_alone (M5, ao) DROPS to <= ceiling (frozen baseline ~0.99); grounding made O materially state-dependent. Low-noise and reproducible (unlike M6).
preconditions.control: ARM_0 (frozen) stays ~0.99; ARM_2 (shuffled, unfittable) also stays ~0.99

preconditions.name: arm1_state_dependence_paired_drop
preconditions.description: median(ARM_0 M5 - ARM_1 M5) -- paired within-seed state-dependence gain from grounding, removing the seed baseline.
preconditions.control: ARM_0 is the same substrate with a frozen head

preconditions.name: content_not_traffic_discriminated
preconditions.description: median(ARM_2 M5 - ARM_1 M5) -- TRUE-effect grounding is state-dependent while the SHUFFLED control is not (its target is unfittable). Confirms the manipulation is world-effect CONTENT, not gradient traffic.
preconditions.control: ARM_2 = same objective + traffic on shuffled targets

gate_detail.m6_note: M6 (within-pair consequence spearman) is recorded but NOT gated: calibration showed the frozen ao head's M6 varies -0.18..+0.13 by seed and world_forward's own M6 is 0.07-0.22, so an absolute M6 floor is not usable on the 16-dim ao head.

interpretation.summary: Grounding O in the world-effect took (M5 median=0.7247, fit MSE=0.7726, ARM_2-ARM_1 M5 margin=0.2750) but did NOT change behaviour (ARM_1 harm_rate=0.5144 vs ARM_0=0.4426, ARM_2=0.4209). SD-004's semantic-grounding efficiency rationale is demoted; SD-080 stays candidate as a correctness-not-capability finding.
